extracted.intended_audience: foreign patent applicants and their counsel preparing or prosecuting patent applications in China
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and prosecuting patent applications before the China National Intellectual Property Administration (CNIPA) under the 2026 Examination Guidelines, with emphasis on inventiveness, amendments, support/clarity, and AI/emerging-technology handling. Focuses on practical drafting and prosecution steps foreign applicants should take to improve grant prospects.

rubrics_metrics.name: More Clarification on Inventiveness Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Refinement of how inventiveness is evaluated, especially for algorithm-related inventions, software solutions, and business-related technical features. Inventiveness objections focus on whether a feature makes a technical contribution to the solution of a technical problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guidelines provide structured explanations on: how technical features are identified; how distinguishing features should be analyzed; how technical effects are determined. Practical drafting implications: simply emphasizing 'improved performance' or 'better efficiency' in a general way may not be sufficient. Applicants should clearly describe what technical problem is being solved; which specific technical means are used; and what technical effect is directly achieved. For PCT-route filings entering China, ensure technical effects are not only mentioned in background/summary but are supported in the detailed description with concrete embodiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tighter Standards on Amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Further clarification of the boundaries of permissible amendments during substantive examination, particularly relating to addition of new technical features, combination of embodiments, and extraction of features from examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes application of Article 33 (added matter): any amendment must be clearly and directly derivable from the original disclosure. Practical consequences: claim drafting at the filing stage becomes more critical; relying on broad, generic disclosure to support later narrowing amendments may be risky. The Guidelines suggest intermediate generalizations introduced during prosecution can trigger added-matter objections; such objections may become more common.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increasing Attention to Support and Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Stronger emphasis on the support requirement and clarity of claims during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners are encouraged to examine whether claims are fully supported by the description; assess whether functional features are sufficiently defined; and review whether technical terms are clearly explained. For foreign-origin applications (especially translated from English), extra care is required to ensure the description supports the claims and that functional language and technical terminology are clearly and unambiguously presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on AI-Related and Emerging Technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: More detailed guidance on examination of AI-related inventions and other emerging technologies, while maintaining the core requirement that the invention must solve a technical problem using technical means to produce a technical effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI-related inventions are not treated as a special category — the standard remains: solve a technical problem, use technical means, produce a technical effect. Explanatory examples are expanded to show how examiners may analyze such cases. Practical drafting advice for AI/data-processing/intelligent-systems: describe hardware interaction where applicable; clearly link algorithms to specific technical applications; avoid presenting purely abstract data processing without technical context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical Drafting & Prosecution Recommendations for Overseas Applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Actionable suggestions for foreign applicants to improve examination outcomes under the revised Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft with potential Chinese examination standards in mind, especially regarding technical effects. Avoid relying solely on functional claim language. Ensure sufficient fallback positions are explicitly disclosed in the description. Pay attention to translation quality and adaptation (not just literal accuracy). Overall, claim drafting at filing stage is critical to withstand stricter amendment and support scrutiny; anticipate that small clarifications in the Guidelines can influence day-to-day examination practice (stricter formal compliance, more structured inventiveness analysis, closer scrutiny of claim wording).
